title: ₹250 Ka Cappuccino: Cafe Owner Ko Kitna Bachta Hai?
description: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. Cafes are a very common dream business for men aged 18 to 34, and the pizza franchise reel already shows that a franchise unit-economics breakdown works. The low raw-material cost against a high menu price makes a curiosity hook that gets shared.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: Per-cup economics of an Indian cafe (as of 9 Nov 2026)

**READ FIRST: the hook needs a tweak**
- Several guides say a cappuccino costs ₹20–25 to make and sells for ₹150–180. [https://www.restaurantindia.in/article/cafe-business-in-india-setup-cost-profit-margins-what-nobody-tells-you.16054] I found no source for a ₹250 cup with ₹20–25 of coffee.
- Other sources put ingredient cost higher. One example is a ₹220 cappuccino costing ₹50–60 in ingredients. [https://www.restaurantindia.in/article/cafe-business-in-india-setup-cost-profit-margins-what-nobody-tells-you.16054] Another puts in-house cost at ₹30–45 for a ₹140–220 cappuccino. [https://trufflenationonline.com/blog/how-to-open-cafe-india/]
- Safer script: "coffee + milk is only about 13% of the price" (₹180 example below). Real ingredient cost is higher once cup, sugar and wastage are added.
- Prices at the top end do exist. Starbucks charges ₹215 for a solo espresso. [https://instacuppastore.com/blogs/main-page/the-real-cost-of-home-espresso-in-india-machine-grinder-beans-maintenance-per-cup-math] Independent cafes charge ₹130–180 for a latte or cappuccino. [same URL]

**1. Cup cost: the ₹180 cappuccino (one roaster's worked example)**
- Coffee is about ₹13.50, or 7.5% of the price, for a 9 g single shot at ₹1,500/kg. [https://www.tinytigercoffee.in/blogs/journal/cafe-coffee-cost-per-cup]
- Milk (150 ml full cream at ₹70/litre) adds ₹10.50, so coffee and milk together are about 13% of the price. [same URL]
- That leaves ₹156, or 86.7% of the price, for everything else. [same URL]
- A double shot takes ingredient cost to about 21%. [same URL]
- This source is a coffee roaster, so treat it as an example, not an audit.
- Toned milk in Delhi NCR is about ₹58–66/litre. [https://brootcoffee.com/pages/cafe-cost-calculator]
- A healthy Indian cafe runs beverage cost of goods at 18–28% of menu price. [https://brootcoffee.com/pages/cafe-cost-calculator]
- Wholesale roasted beans start around ₹700/kg. Specialty beans cost roughly ₹1,200–2,600/kg. [https://www.tinytigercoffee.in/blogs/journal/wholesale-coffee-beans-price-per-kg-india]
- Specialty beans at ₹800–2,500/kg work out to ₹15–40 per cup. [https://www.dineopen.com/blog/how-to-start-cafe-coffee-shop-india.html]
- Paper cup: ₹1.50–2.00 single-wall, ₹2.50–4.00 double-wall. [https://successmarketingkota.com/blog/coffee-cup-sizes-guide-for-cafes.html] This page is old (about 642 days), so prices may have moved.
- Ingredient cost by drink:
  - Espresso/Americano: ₹18–30
  - Cappuccino/Latte: ₹30–45
  - In-house cold coffee: ₹35–60 [https://trufflenationonline.com/blog/how-to-open-cafe-india/]

**2. Where the rest of the rupee goes (full P&L)**
- Sample ₹10,00,000 monthly revenue:
  - Food and beverage cost is 30% (₹3,00,000), labour 28% (₹2,80,000) and rent 15% (₹1,50,000).
  - The cafe keeps about ₹1 lakh, a 10% net margin. [https://www.restaurantindia.in/article/cafe-business-in-india-setup-cost-profit-margins-what-nobody-tells-you.16054]
- Scriptwriter's arithmetic from those percentages (not a sourced figure): that leaves about 17% for electricity, royalty, marketing and other costs.
- Per ₹100 of sales on that sample: ₹30 ingredients, ₹28 staff, ₹15 rent, about ₹17 other, about ₹10 profit. Check the maths before putting it on screen.
- Another mid-size cafe example:
  - COGS is ₹1,20,000–1,80,000 (30%).
  - Rent is ₹50,000–80,000 (15%).
  - Staff is ₹70,000–1,20,000 (18%) for 4–6 people.
  - Net profit is ₹40,000–90,000 (about 10–15%). [https://www.dineopen.com/blog/how-to-start-cafe-coffee-shop-india.html]
- Industry guideline: F&B cost under 35%, labour under 30%, occupancy

SOURCES:
https://www.tinytigercoffee.in/blogs/journal/cafe-coffee-cost-per-cup
https://www.restaurantindia.in/article/cafe-business-in-india-setup-cost-profit-margins-what-nobody-tells-you.16054
